title: Hosted API demo - chat/text generation basics
summary: AE + SE ran a hosted API walkthrough focused on chat/text generation basics: streaming responses, key parameters (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop), retry/Idempotency guidance, and demo of the Console. Customer asked about latency, data retention, SOC2, and how retries/at-most-once semantics work. Agreed next steps: share pricing + trial account, security docs, and run a short benchmark using their prompt set.
topics: Generation params: temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences
Console demo: model selection + streaming toggle
action_items: Maya Chen: send pricing and trial instructions (due 2026-03-24)
Diego Alvarez: share sample benchmark script and suggested load config (due 2026-03-26)
Priya Menon / AeroHealth: share 5 representative prompts and desired latency SLOs (due 2026-03-25)
Maya Chen: attach SOC2 + security whitepaper link (due 2026-03-24)
next_steps: Redwood to provision trial API keys for AeroHealth sandbox
Run 1k-request benchmark against hosted API with customer's prompts
Follow-up meeting week of 2026-03-30 to review benchmark and discuss Dedicated if needed
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-03-22 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Menon (AeroHealth Head of Data), Carlos Ruiz (AeroHealth Eng Manager), Sam Lee (AeroHealth Security)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, i have Diego (SE) with me. how's everyone's afternoon?
[00:06] Dr. Priya Menon: hi Maya, good thanks, excited to see this, we wanted to focus on the hosted api and basic chat generation patterns.
[00:12] Carlos Ruiz: yeah and really curious about streaming and retries, we have tight latency SLOs so want to understand tradeoffs.
[00:18] Maya Chen: great, that's what we'll hit. quick agenda: overview of hosted API, demo in the console and SDK, streaming + params, then Q&A and next steps. sound good?
[00:27] Carlos Ruiz: yep
[00:30] Diego Alvarez: cool, i'll start with a quick diagram while i share screen \u0014 so redwood's hosted api is a simple REST/SDK layer over our inference runtime, supports chat and text endpoints, embeddings etc. the key for chat is we stream token deltas back to clients using server-sent events or streaming chunks in our SDKs.
[00:45] Diego Alvarez: (mumble) so when you call /v1/chat, you can set stream=true and you'll get incremental chunks, which reduces TTF-first-token and improves perceived latency.
[00:55] Sam Lee: is stream implemented as SSE or websockets?
[01:00] Diego Alvarez: mostly SSE and HTTP chunked responses, our JS and Python SDKs wrap that so it's just an async iterator for you. websockets are on our roadmap but not necessary for most workloads.
[01:09] Dr. Priya Menon: and if a stream drops mid-response, do you have retry semantics or do we have to re-request full context?
[01:16] Diego Alvarez: good question \u0014 we recommend idempotency keys for non-streamed requests; for streams specifically, the client should handle reconnects. we do support resumable streaming for some models by reusing the conversation state (you pass the prior messages and the partial token offset). it's not magical, but you can continue from the last valid token.
[01:31] Maya Chen: important point: for deterministic retry behavior on generate calls, our SDKs expose an idempotency-key header. if you re-run the same request with the same key, we ensure at-most-once billing and try to return the same response when possible; there are edge cases with non-deterministic models.
[01:47] Carlos Ruiz: ok so idempotency helps billing and duplicate output?
[01:50] Maya Chen: yes, helps billing and reduces duplicate side-effects, but for exactly-once semantics you'd want to combine idempotent calls with server-side dedupe of downstream actions.
[01:59] Diego Alvarez: moving to params: temperature, top_p, max_tokens \u0014 temperature controls randomness, top_p is nucleus sampling. we showed earlier benchmarks where lowering temperature reduced variance but also reduced creativity.
[02:13] Dr. Priya Menon: what's a good starting point for customer support style responses?
[02:17] Diego Alvarez: usually temperature 0.0-0.3, max_tokens tuned to the expected response length, and use stop sequences to avoid model rambling. we often recommend temperature 0.0 for deterministic extractions.
[02:30] Carlos Ruiz: what about top_p vs temperature, do you recommend using both?
[02:34] Diego Alvarez: they can be complementary \u0014 many teams keep temperature and top_p default and tune one at a time. top_p 0.9 is common.
[02:42] Maya Chen: also highlight prompt engineering: prefix instructions, role tokens, and system messages in chat endpoints \u0014 small changes can noticeably affect output length and tokens.
[02:52] Dr. Priya Menon: when you say tokens, we're charged per token both input and output right?
[02:56] Maya Chen: correct; hosted billing is per input and output token. console shows token breakdown per call which helps debugging cost.
[03:04] Diego Alvarez: now I'm going to demo the console quick \u0014 model catalog, you can see redwood-3b, redwood-7b-quant, and curated open models with performance notes. i'll toggle to stream so you can see incremental output.
[03:18] [screen share noises] Diego Alvarez: okay typing a prompt \u0014 \"You are a helpful assistant summarizing clinical notes\" \u0014 hit send with stream=true \u0014 you'll see response arrive chunk by chunk.
[03:29] Carlos Ruiz: wow that looks snappy. what's typical first token latency?
[03:33] Diego Alvarez: depends on model and size, for 7B quant models we typically see 80\u0013150ms first-token on nvidia a100 pools in hosted; smaller models can be <50ms. we also have warm pools for pinned customers.
[03:46] Sam Lee: do you provide SLA for latency on hosted?
[03:49] Maya Chen: hosted is best-effort with transparent benchmarks; SLA-backed latency is offered on Dedicated. we can discuss a pilot with throughput commitments if you need predictable latency.
[03:58] Dr. Priya Menon: security: data retention, encryption at rest, SOC2 \u2014 can you summarize?
[04:03] Maya Chen: yes, short: data in flight TLS, at-rest encryption via customer-managed keys available for private deployments, hosted uses KMS-managed keys. we retain logs for X days by default (we can configure retention and opt-out of retention for enterprise). we are SOC2 Type II compliant \u2014 i'll send the whitepaper.
[04:18] Sam Lee: do you support SSO / SAML and RBAC?
[04:21] Maya Chen: yes, SSO/SAML, SCIM, and fine-grained RBAC in the Console.
[04:27] Carlos Ruiz: back to retries: if we set automatic retries in our client when a 5xx happens, will it double-charge us?
[04:33] Diego Alvarez: if retry happens and the original request actually succeeded but the ack was lost, you could get double side-effects. idempotency-key header mitigates billing duplicates. we also recommend client-side exponential backoff and jitter.
[04:45] Dr. Priya Menon: any tips on batching for cost-savings?
[04:48] Diego Alvarez: yes, batching multiple prompts into one request or using our prefix cache for repeated contexts saves tokens and reduces per-token overhead. Redwood Optimize will suggest batch sizes based on your traffic shape.
[04:58] Maya Chen: quick note on throttling: we enforce rate limits and quotas. console shows your current usage and helps set quota alerts.
[05:05] Carlos Ruiz: can we pin model versions? we need behavior stability.
[05:09] Diego Alvarez: absolutely \u2014 you can pin a model version and rollout via canary or A/B. model catalog shows version hashes.
[05:16] Dr. Priya Menon: can you show an example of adjusting temperature live?
[05:19] Diego Alvarez: sure \u2014 changing temp from 0.2 to 0.8 in console \u2014 you can see responses get longer and more varied. sometimes useful for brainstorming features vs deterministic extraction.
[05:32] [small crosstalk; typing]
[05:40] Sam Lee: quick question on logs: are transcripts stored in plaintext? we need to know for PHI handling.
[05:45] Maya Chen: by default logs are retained for debugging but you can opt-out or set short retention windows; for PHI we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with customer-managed keys and disable retention. we'll include the security doc.
[05:58] Carlos Ruiz: what about retries for streaming specifically \u2014 if stream disconnects after 60 tokens, do you prefer re-requesting full context?
[06:05] Diego Alvarez: re-requesting the conversation history (messages) and passing last-known partial tokens is the practical approach. some teams buffer partial output client-side and resume. with small responses, re-request is fine.
[06:18] Dr. Priya Menon: how do you handle long context window models \u2014 do you evict KV cache?
[06:23] Diego Alvarez: our runtime manages KV cache; if you're using long-context models we recommend quantized variants and be mindful of prompt size. caching prefixes (like patient history preamble) as a static prefix reduces repeated compute.
[06:36] Maya Chen: ok switching gears \u2014 SDK patterns. our python SDK sample: client.chat.create(messages=[...], temperature=0.0, max_tokens=256, stream=True). iterate async for chunk in response: print(chunk.delta). error handling built in to raise on 4xx/5xx.
[06:52] Carlos Ruiz: is there a retries helper in SDK?
[06:55] Diego Alvarez: yes, SDK has a RetryPolicy object; it's configurable for idempotency, max attempts, and backoff. default is 3 attempts with exponential backoff.
[07:05] Sam Lee: will retry policy retry on rate limit (429)?
[07:08] Diego Alvarez: yes, with Retry-After respected. for 429 we recommend exponential backoff and consider queueing at the client side for bursty loads.
[07:17] Dr. Priya Menon: can we get transcript logs of calls for debugging?
[07:21] Maya Chen: yes, audit logs and request-level traces are available in console; we redact secrets and can configure retention.
[07:28] Maya Chen: any other questions on usage patterns?
[07:31] Carlos Ruiz: curious about cost \u2014 can you give a ballpark for 7B quant vs 3B?
[07:36] Maya Chen: rough numbers: 3B is cheaper per token and lower latency; 7B quant gives better quality for few extra ms/cost. exact pricing depends on commit/volume \u2014 i'll include a pricing sheet.
[07:45] Dr. Priya Menon: what are typical steps to go from trial to production?
[07:49] Maya Chen: trial keys -> run benchmark with your prompts -> evaluate quality and latency -> if you need predictability sign a Dedicated reserved capacity or enterprise contract -> we help with pinning and rollout policies.
[07:59] Diego Alvarez: last demo bit: retries with idempotency key example in node: const key = uuid(); client.chat.create({messages, idempotencyKey: key}).then... this helps avoid double-side effects.
[08:12] [pause / typing]
[08:20] Sam Lee: if we run a benchmark, what should be in the env? VPC?
[08:24] Maya Chen: for initial tests use hosted sandbox keys; if you need VPC/pinned capacity we can provision a Dedicated trial. for PHI use Dedicated/private.
[08:33] Carlos Ruiz: ok let's confirm next steps \u2014 we'll share prompts and SLOs, Redwood will provision sandbox keys and run a 1k-request benchmark with suggested settings?
[08:41] Maya Chen: yes. Diego will prepare a sample script showing temperature/top_p permutations and suggested backoff for retries.
[08:48] Dr. Priya Menon: timeline? we want results by next week.
[08:51] Maya Chen: we'll aim for results before 2026-03-30 and meet same week.
[08:56] [closing pleasantries]
[09:02] Maya Chen: thanks everyone for the time, i'll follow up with the deck, pricing, and SOC2.
[09:06] Carlos Ruiz: thanks Maya, Diego.
[09:08] Dr. Priya Menon: thanks all.
[09:10] [call ends]
